sections.title: 4 · 下周展望
sections.body: The read into next week is a duration rotation, not risk-off. Capital left the most rate- and vol-sensitive long-duration tech capex names and went into a supply-driven real-asset theme that ignores the discount rate — the el-nino-ag row ran the widest single-week excess in the book. The vol row is the one to watch: a bid into a hiking FOMC is hedging demand with no policy cushion, and it punishes the longest-dated equity cash flows first. Cloud/Hyperscaler sits in that firing line. Software/SaaS and Devices/Endpoint showed the selling was selective, not systemic, so the question next week is whether the equipment de-rate spreads to the broader complex or stays contained. Watch whether the vol bid extends or fades, and whether the front-end policy path holds its hike odds through the 9/16 meeting.

oneThing.body: Yesterday: no prior checks. Volatility, not rates, was the loudest signal today. A VIX pushing 16-17 into a hiking meeting is the tell — hedging demand rising while the policy path offers no cushion. Ranked by cash-flow duration, the longest-dated equity cash flows are hurt first: Semi-Cap/EDA and Cloud/Hyperscaler, the names whose value sits furthest out the curve, are what a vol bid and a 4.79 ten-year punish hardest — and the tape confirmed it below.
